decisionsTitle: The backoffice's status chip: the public glyph table keeps only public names
decisionsSection:
**Why.** §694 made `GlyphChip` the one chip and left about a dozen names in the public glyph table (`modules/events/ui/glyphs.ts`) that only the backoffice draws, so every visitor's bundle carried backoffice icons. The owner's standing rule is fast and clean; the header and the landing page are what every visitor pays for (`AGENTS.md` §1.5). This amends §694 (the one chip stays the rule for public pages and the shop) and §521 (the icon guard's registries).

**Decision.** The backoffice has its own chip, `StatusChip` (`src/shared/ui/StatusChip.tsx`), with its own registry `src/shared/ui/status-glyphs.ts`, one file per glyph (§90). The look is `GlyphChip`'s: small, the palette's colour tokens, the glyph before the words; it has no tooltip, link or screen-reader extras. The names it holds: `done`, `cancelled`, `open`, `planned`, `building` (a state's or a plan's step), `visible`, `hidden`, `language` (a row shown or hidden, a one-language text), `shop`, `link`, and `series` (a repeated event's count, §113, drawn only by the backoffice's event list and the design page). Their call sites are the team page and its boxes, the shop's product page in the backoffice, the event list and the design page. `person` stays public (the team card's fold); `GlyphSelect` and the staff preview draw public names and stay on `GlyphChip`'s table.

**What stays public for now.** Two kinds of name stay in the public table. `done`, `cancelled` and `planned` stay for good: the members' zone's order chip (`src/app/[locale]/members-area/MembersShop.tsx`) is public and draws them through `GlyphChip`, while the backoffice's states draw them through `StatusChip`, so they sit in both tables (`BOTH_SURFACES` in the tripwire; each table imports its own icon file, and a visitor downloads only the public one). `visible`, `hidden`, `language`, `orders` and `club` stay for now: the backoffice shop's orders card and product list (`src/modules/content/shop/ui/OrdersCard.tsx`, `ProductList.tsx`, rendered by `/admin/shop` alone) draw them through `GlyphChip`, and another change owns those files; this change does not touch them. They are listed as `PENDING_SHOP` in the tripwire, which fails the day the shop stops drawing one, so the list cannot rot. Moving those two files to `StatusChip`, with `orders` and `club` added to `status-glyphs.ts`, takes the five out of the public table; that is a later change (QUEUE «Later»). The members' zone never moves to `StatusChip`: the tripwire refuses it there.

**A server chip or an island?** The server chip was tried first, in thought: MUI's `Chip` is a client component, so an `icon={<Icon />}` made in a Server Component reaches it as a lazy Flight reference, `isValidElement` says no and hydration fails (§370, the defect `GlyphChip` records). `GlyphButton` and `panel-glyphs` can draw a glyph server-side only because the glyph is a child, not a prop of a client MUI component. A chip that keeps MUI's `Chip` look cannot, so `StatusChip` is a second small client island that takes a name and makes the element on its own side; the cost is one island whose table holds eleven icons rather than the public one's forty.

**The tripwire.** `tests/unit/design/status-chip.test.ts`: the two tables share no name but the members' zone's three and the shop's pending five; no public file imports `StatusChip` or `status-glyphs.ts`; every status name is drawn by a file that imports `StatusChip`; every plain public name is drawn by a public file. The public files are what the house's `isBackoffice` classifier (`guards-allowlist.ts`) does not call backoffice, plus the six team-page components a visitor renders (`TeamCanvas`, `TeamCanvasBox`, `TeamCanvasCard`, `TeamMemberLinks`, `TeamPhotoImage`, `TeamLinkGlyph` under `content/team/ui/`); the team's editors and the whole event editor (`content/events/`) stay backoffice, and the members' zone stays public. The registries and `StatusChip` itself are neither. A name counts as drawn only where a file really draws it, read from the parsed tree so a comment never counts: a `glyph` attribute on `GlyphChip`, `ChipLink` or `StatusChip` (never a Panel's or a button's, which have their own tables); a `glyph` property of an object declared with the registry's type (a variable's annotation, a `satisfies`/`as`, or the return type of the function returning it, naming `GlyphName`/`StatusGlyphName` exactly or a type of the file whose `glyph` member does, such as `route-pills.ts`'s `Pill`); a table typed `Record<…, GlyphName>`; and `GLYPHS.<name>` / `STATUS_GLYPHS["name"]` only where the file imports that table from its registry (or is the registry), never a local table of the same name (`AskFirstButton`, `MenuOrderList`). Probes plant regressions in sources made from text, parsed as the scan parses the real ones: a public file drawing `series` through `GlyphChip` puts it in the public set; a Panel's `glyph`, a comment and an untyped `{ glyph }` object draw nothing; a local `GLYPHS` is not the registry; a members' zone file importing `StatusChip` is an offender; the event editor and the team's editors are not public; a backoffice file drawing a name in neither table stays out of the public set. `status-glyphs.ts` is an icon registry in `guards-allowlist.ts`; the ratchet's numbers do not move. `/admin/design` → «Iconografie» shows the new table with its count, and its primitives rule names `StatusChip`.

**Refused.** One registry for both chips (it is the thing that sent backoffice icons to visitors); a second icon family; moving `GlyphChip`'s tooltip and link features into the new chip (nothing in the backoffice uses them); editing the shop's files in this change.
changelogLine: - **Visitors download fewer icons** — the backoffice's status chips have their own small registry (`StatusChip`), so backoffice-only glyphs leave the public chip's table; nothing changes on screen. §NNN.

specsCriteria.text: The public glyph table (`modules/events/ui/glyphs.ts`) and the backoffice's (`shared/ui/status-glyphs.ts`) share no name except the three the members' zone draws (`done`, `cancelled`, `planned`) and the backoffice shop's listed pending ones, no public file imports `StatusChip` or its registry, and every name of either table is drawn, by a real chip `glyph` use, a registry-typed object or the imported registry read by name, in a file of its own surface, bar the backoffice shop's listed pending names, which the backoffice shop must still draw; planted regressions in synthetic sources are caught (2026-10-11, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).
